notes: Every survival BuildCraft item in this port apart from fluid buckets and the map location is crafted, so its value comes from its recipe: gears, the wrench, engines, machines (including the distiller, the heat exchanger and the builders machines: filler, builder, architect table, electronic library and replacer), blank templates, blueprints and single block schematics, the tank, land and path marks, the marker connector, waterproof, paintbrushes, the zone planner, all pipes (including the structure pipe and the shapeless recipes that turn fluid and kinesis pipes back into item pipes), and the pipe plug and power adapter.

The robot, redstone board and docking station are crafted, so their values come from their recipes; a robot's board and energy are NBT, which transmutation strips, so it pays out an empty robot. The picker, carrier, lumberjack, miner, harvester, leaf cutter, shovelman, breaker, farmer, planter, pump, tank, knight, butcher and stripes boards are programmed in the assembly table, so each is restated as a conversion from a redstone board and its ingredient with laser power left unvalued. Installing or removing a board in the crafting grid is a special recipe that moves NBT, which neither EMC mod maps.

Gates, the gate copier, pipe wire, lenses and filters, the pipe pulsar, the timer and facades come from the assembly table, which ProjectE and Item Alchemy do not map, so each assembly recipe is restated as a conversion with laser power left unvalued. Basic gates and the iron and nether brick gates and iron lapis and quartz gates also have crafting recipes, and the one-item recipes that swap a gate between AND and OR give both logics the same value; where assembly is cheaper, the conversion sets the value so that assembling a gate and transmuting it gains nothing. A facade is one item for every block: its value is the cheapest full block, dirt, plus three structure pipes, divided by the six facades the recipe makes. That counts the copied block and stays below one, so six facades of a diamond block cannot pay out the diamond block. The crafting swap that flips hollow is the same item, and transmutation strips the block NBT.

The mining well, quarry and pump take blocks and fluids from the world for power alone, as a player with a pickaxe or bucket would; they consume no items, so there is no item process to check for EMC gain.

Oil generates in wells and regrows above large wells' springs, so it is a base fluid valued like lava. Every refinery route to light fuel turns a bucket of oil into half a bucket of light fuel: crude oil distils into heavy oil, and hot oil into mixed light fuels, each of which yields light fuel after heating or cooling. Light fuel is therefore worth the two buckets of oil it takes, ignoring the lava and water that heat and cool it, so no route can make it for less. The other refinery fluids are by-products or intermediate heats of that chain and stay unvalued: each distillation turns one fluid into more volume of two others, so valuing those as well would let a split create EMC.

buildcraft:oil_bucket.why: Oil is a worldgen fluid, pumped or bucketed from oil wells and regrowing above large wells' springs, as lava is a worldgen fluid.

conversions.name: refine_light_fuel
conversions.why: The refinery's routes all yield half a bucket of light fuel per bucket of oil, so a bucket of light fuel is worth the oil from two buckets, returning one bucket. The lava and water that heat and cool it, and the by-products, are left out so that no route makes light fuel for less than its value.

conversions.name: recordings_are_worth_their_blanks
conversions.why: The architect table records an area onto a blank template or blueprint, and a blank single block schematic records the block it is used on; each hands back the recorded item, so a recorded item is worth its blank. Transmutation never copies NBT, and a recorded item without its data acts as a blank one: the table records onto a template or blueprint again, and a single block schematic used while sneaking is wiped back to a blank.

conversions.name: assemble_redstone_chipset
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a redstone chipset from a redstone dust and laser power (upstream's chipset assembly recipe). ProjectE and ItemAlchemy map no assembly recipes, so it is restated here; laser power is left unvalued, as engine fuel is.

conversions.name: assemble_ingot_chipsets
conversions.why: The assembly table makes iron and golden chipsets from a redstone dust, an ingot of their metal and laser power, which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_quartz_chipset
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a quartz chipset from a redstone dust, a nether quartz and laser power, which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_diamond_chipset
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a diamond chipset from a redstone dust, a diamond and laser power, which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_iron_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table makes iron AND and OR gates from an iron chipset and laser power (upstream BCSiliconRecipes), far cheaper than crafting one from iron ingots, so the crafting recipe cannot price them above what assembly pays.

conversions.name: assemble_nether_brick_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table makes nether brick AND and OR gates from an iron chipset, a nether brick block and laser power.

conversions.name: assemble_gold_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table makes gold AND and OR gates, which have no crafting recipe, from a golden chipset and laser power.

conversions.name: assemble_lapis_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table adds a lapis modifier to an unmodified gate of the same material and logic with one lapis lazuli and laser power; crafting an iron lapis gate takes four.

conversions.name: assemble_quartz_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table adds a quartz modifier to an unmodified gate of the same material and logic with a quartz chipset and laser power; crafting an iron quartz gate takes four nether quartz.

conversions.name: assemble_diamond_gates
conversions.why: The assembly table adds a diamond modifier, which has no crafting recipe, to an unmodified gate of the same material and logic with a diamond chipset and laser power.

conversions.name: assemble_gate_copier
conversions.why: The assembly table makes the gate copier from a wrench, an iron chipset and laser power. Transmutation never copies NBT, so a copier is valued as an empty one.

conversions.name: assemble_pipe_wire
conversions.why: The assembly table makes eight pipe wire of one colour from a redstone dust, a dye of that colour and laser power (upstream BCTransportRecipes), which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_lenses
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a lens from a stained glass block of its colour and laser power (upstream BCSiliconRecipes), which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_filters
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a filter from a stained glass block of its colour, iron bars and laser power, which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_clear_lens
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a clear lens from any glass block and laser power; upstream's blockGlass includes stained glass, and plain glass is the cheapest.

conversions.name: assemble_clear_filter
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a clear filter from any glass block, iron bars and laser power; plain glass is the cheapest.

conversions.name: assemble_pulsar
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a pipe pulsar from a redstone engine, two iron ingots and laser power (upstream BCSiliconRecipes), which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_board_picker
conversions.why: The assembly table programs a redstone board into the picker robot board with a hopper and laser power (this port's clean-room robots), which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_timer

conversions.name: assemble_light_sensor
conversions.why: The assembly table makes a light sensor from a daylight detector and laser power (upstream BCSiliconRecipes), which is left unvalued.

conversions.name: assemble_facades
conversions.why: The assembly table makes six facades from one block and three structure pipes (upstream FacadeAssemblyRecipes), with laser power left unvalued. One item id covers every block, and transmutation strips NBT, so the value is this cheapest recipe: dirt, a full block, plus the pipes, divided by six. Six facades therefore cannot be worth more than the block they were made from.

exclude.buildcraft:frame: Creative-only: the quarry builds its frame from power, frame blocks drop nothing, and there is no frame recipe, so a value would only make creative frames transmutable.
exclude.buildcraft:oil_spring: Creative-only: the spring under large oil wells is unbreakable like bedrock and drops nothing; the oil it regrows is what gets a value.
exclude.buildcraft:water_spring: Creative-only: upstream never generates water springs, and the block is unbreakable like bedrock and drops nothing; a value would only make an infinite water source transmutable.
exclude.buildcraft:volume_box: Creative-only: upstream has no recipe for the volume box, and its boxes are free-standing marks rather than material, so a value would only make a creative item transmutable.
exclude.buildcraft:map_location: No recipe: upstream's map location is filled by using it on a block, and the zone planner only reads and writes that NBT. Transmutation never copies NBT, so a value would pay out a blank map.
exclude.buildcraft:fragile_fluid_shard: NBT item: a shard only holds the fluid a broken machine or pipe dropped, and a blank shard holds nothing and cannot be filled. Transmutation never copies NBT, so a value could only be paid out for an empty, useless shard.

refinery_fluid_buckets.why: Refinery by-products and intermediate heats: each distillation turns one fluid into more volume of two others, so only oil and light fuel, the chain's input and goal, are valued. Leaving residue unvalued also keeps the residue-to-waterproof recipe from pricing waterproof.

processes.name: refine_light_fuel_through_heavy_oil
processes.why: The cheapest route: 8 oil distils into 3 heavy oil (and 16 gaseous fuel); lava heats the heavy oil, which distils into 4 hot light fuel (and 2 dense oil), and water cools it. The unvalued by-products are left out.

processes.name: assemble_facades_do_not_gain
processes.why: Six facades are one item id, valued from dirt. Crafting them from dirt, glass or a diamond block and transmuting the six must not return more than that block.

processes.name: refine_light_fuel_through_mixed_light_fuels
processes.why: Upstream's documented route: lava heats 4 oil, which distils into 5 hot mixed light fuels (and 1 dense oil); water cools them and they distil into 2 light fuel (and 8 gaseous fuel). The unvalued by-products are left out.
